title: Illustration / Characters / Arms and hands
slide_intent: Use only the hand detail needed for a gesture so the pose remains clear and feasible to produce repeatedly.
strategic_value: Abstract hands can help Duolingo preserve expressive action without increasing illustration and animation complexity unnecessarily.
demonstration: A tall grid shows arm positions, prop-holding poses, translucent construction views, gestures and isolated hand shapes; text at right explains simplification.
practical_value: Start with circular hands and add only the fingers required to make the specific pose readable.

content_islands.name: Pose and construction studies
content_islands.spec: Group standing arm positions and prop interactions at upper left, followed by blue construction views and gesture examples.

content_islands.name: Hand-shape specimens
content_islands.spec: Place the isolated hand silhouettes at the bottom of the visual field, comparing simple circles and a few explicit fingers.

content_islands.name: Production rationale
content_islands.spec: Set Arms and Hands and its paragraph at right, explaining the time cost of posing and animation.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text identifies arms and hands as time-consuming for illustrators and animators and connects abstraction with easier production.
reference_purposes.Expression: The examples maintain a simple rounded hand vocabulary across varied gestures.
reference_purposes.Application: The grid demonstrates circular hands, prop interactions and selectively visible fingers.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The source asks for the minimum fingers needed for the pose and circular abstraction in most situations.

ingredient.name: Abstract hands
ingredient.role: Make gestures readable with minimal construction.
ingredient.application: Keep hands circular in most situations and display only the fingers needed for the pose.
ingredient.scope: Historical official Duolingo illustration guidance from the 2024–2025 archived snapshot. This page states a minimum-detail principle; the explicit four-finger maximum appears in the following prohibition panel.
